correction.text: Cambodia from its independence from France on 9 November 1953

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria draws Cambodia inside French Indochina in 1953-1955 and starts the Kingdom in 1956. 'Cambodia achieved independence from France under Norodom Sihanouk' on 9 November 1953; the page gives no boundary, so the 1956 outline is borrowed.

184,307 km2 for 1956-1966 against the infobox 181,035 km2 (ratio 1.02): the outline matches modern Cambodia (622 of its 623 grid cells). Preah Vihear is 'unsettled since 1962' on the page, with no change drawn.

correction.text: the whole of Cambodia; the north-eastern corner stays Cambodian in 1967-1972

keyframe_review.note: 179,992 km2 for 1967-1972: Cliopatria drops 13 grid cells (about 3,300 km2, 107.0-107.6 E, 13.7-14.3 N) in the north-east. In 1967 'the National Front for the Liberation of South Vietnam recognized the inviolability of Cambodia's borders ... and North Vietnam quickly followed', and in 1965 a deal let Viet Cong and North Vietnamese forces 'build permanent military facilities on Cambodian soil'; the pages give no cession. The corner is restored and the Vietnamese-held north-east of 1970-1972 is carried as a hatched occupation event.

correction.text: the whole of Cambodia held by the Khmer Republic and the insurgents, 1973-1975

keyframe_review.note: 179,709 km2 for 1973-1975: the 1967 outline less one cell; the same 14 north-eastern cells appear in Cliopatria's Democratic Republic of Vietnam shape of 1973. The Khmer Republic page says only that North Vietnam and the Viet Cong 'had gained de facto control over vast areas of eastern Cambodia' and that the insurgents surrounded Phnom Penh by 1975, with no percentages, so the whole country is kept and the north-east is an event.

correction.text: Cambodia from the restoration of the monarchy on 24 September 1993

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria starts this row in 1996 and keeps the People's Republic of Kampuchea to 1995, although the infobox gives 'Monarchy restored: 24 September 1993' (State of Cambodia 30 April 1989; United Nations Administered Cambodia 28 February 1992). The 1996 outline is used for 1993-1995.

184,307 km2 for 1996-2023, the same outline as 1956 (infobox 181,035 km2, ratio 1.02). The page records no border change; the Thai border dispute that 'escalated into an armed conflict' in 2025 and the 'disagreements over some offshore islands and sections of the boundary with Vietnam' move no line.
Same outline as 1996; the 2025 armed conflict with Thailand is after the shape and moved no border.

ledger.note: 1953: Cambodia becomes independent (9 November). 'Cambodia achieved independence from France under Norodom Sihanouk' (infobox 9 November 1953); the page gives no boundary, so the region is Cliopatria's 1956 outline.

region.text: the north-east: 'seizing large portions of the eastern and northeastern parts of the country'; 'taken all five of Cambodia's northeastern provinces' by April 1970. The page names only Kratie and Ratanakiri; the four provinces drawn (Ratanakiri, Mondulkiri, Stung Treng, Kratie) are the researcher's reading

ledger.note: 1970: North Vietnam takes the north-east. The PAVN offensive (from 29 March 1970) seized 'large portions of the eastern and northeastern parts of the country'; 'After defeating FANK forces, PAVN turned the newly won territories over to local insurgents.' Cliopatria's shape drops only 13 cells there.

region.text: the Parrot's Beak of Svay Rieng Province (Operation Toan Thang 42 crossed on 30 April 1970) and the Fishhook (US forces entered on 1 May) around Snuol; ARVN set 'a depth of 40-60 km' from the border. The radii are the researcher's reading

ledger.note: 1970: South Vietnamese and US forces enter eastern Cambodia (the Cambodian campaign, 29 April to 22 July): ARVN at the Parrot's Beak on 30 April, US forces at the Fishhook on 1 May (withdrawn by 30 June). Infobox: 'Temporary occupation and subsequent withdrawal from eastern Cambodia by ARVN/US'.

region.text: the Parrot's Beak of Svay Rieng Province (Operation Toan Thang 42 crossed on 30 April 1970) and the Fishhook (US forces entered on 1 May) around Snuol; ARVN set 'a depth of 40-60 km' from the border. The radii are the researcher's reading

ledger.note: 1970: the campaign ends (22 July) with the withdrawal of ARVN and US forces; ARVN's zone was later reduced to 'a depth of 10-15 km' (mid-1971).

1970: the monarchy is abolished and the Khmer Republic proclaimed (9 October) by Lon Nol, who had overthrown Sihanouk on 18 March 1970; same state, same colour (rule 2). The Kingdom page: 'the monarchy was abolished in a coup on 9 October 1970'.

region.text: the north-east: 'seizing large portions of the eastern and northeastern parts of the country'; 'taken all five of Cambodia's northeastern provinces' by April 1970. The page names only Kratie and Ratanakiri; the four provinces drawn (Ratanakiri, Mondulkiri, Stung Treng, Kratie) are the researcher's reading

ledger.note: 1972: North Vietnamese forces 'gradually and deliberately scaled back their presence' in Cambodia, leaving the insurgents (CPNLAF, the Khmer Rouge) in the north-east; the Civil War page says the combat was handed to the insurgents ('Khmerization') as their strength reached 35-40,000.

region.text: the north-east: 'seizing large portions of the eastern and northeastern parts of the country'; 'taken all five of Cambodia's northeastern provinces' by April 1970. The page names only Kratie and Ratanakiri; the four provinces drawn (Ratanakiri, Mondulkiri, Stung Treng, Kratie) are the researcher's reading

ledger.note: 1972: the north-east passes to the Khmer Rouge and its fighting with the Republic. The Khmer Rouge also established 'liberated' areas in the south and south-west; the pages give no extent for them or for the countryside.

region.text: the north-east: 'seizing large portions of the eastern and northeastern parts of the country'; 'taken all five of Cambodia's northeastern provinces' by April 1970. The page names only Kratie and Ratanakiri; the four provinces drawn (Ratanakiri, Mondulkiri, Stung Treng, Kratie) are the researcher's reading

ledger.note: 1975: the war ends on 17 April, when Phnom Penh surrendered to the Khmer Rouge.

region.text: the whole of Cambodia: 'The Lon Nol government in Phnom Penh surrendered on 17 April 1975'; the last Republic-held area, the Preah Vihear temple, was taken on 22 May 1975

ledger.note: 1975: Phnom Penh falls to the Khmer Rouge (17 April), after Lon Nol resigned and left on 1 April; the last Republic-held area, the Preah Vihear temple, falls on 22 May. The land belongs to Democratic Kampuchea (Cliopatria's Khmer Rouge row, 1976-1978) and then the People's Republic of Kampuchea (1979-1995).
1993: the monarchy is restored (24 September) as the Kingdom of Cambodia, after the State of Cambodia (30 April 1989) and the United Nations administration (28 February 1992).

region.text: the whole of Cambodia, under the restored monarchy

ledger.note: 1993: Cambodia returns under its king after the UNTAC elections ('Monarchy restored: 24 September 1993'). The People's Republic of Kampuchea row (State of Cambodia from 1989) runs to 1995 in Cliopatria; the region is its 1996 outline.

wars.note: Infobox 2 April 1967 (the Samlaut uprising) to 17 April 1975; Operation Freedom Deal bombing 19 May 1970 to 15 August 1973; Khmer Rouge offensive from 1 January 1975 with about 40,000 troops around the capital by late March.

certainty.note: A colonial-era surveyed frontier; the pages record Cambodia's borders recognised by the National Liberation Front and North Vietnam in 1967.
The war: the north-east and the countryside were held by PAVN and the Khmer Rouge without lines on any page.
The state is absent: the land belongs to Democratic Kampuchea, the People's Republic of Kampuchea and the State of Cambodia (other dossiers).

The page notes disputes with Thailand (Preah Vihear, 'unsettled since 1962'; armed conflict in 2025) and 'disagreements over some offshore islands and sections of the boundary with Vietnam', moving no line.

notes: Wikidata Q424 is shared with the Cliopatria row 'Cambodia' (1700-1802, Cambodia Middle Period; slug cambodia, dossier by another group): they are not merged here, because the two rows are separated by 150 years of Khmer Empire, French protectorate and Indochina rows and this dossier begins with independence from France in 1953; the colour agent may give them one family hue. Cliopatria's row has no shape for 1976-1995: Democratic Kampuchea (khmer-rouge, 1976-78) and the People's Republic of Kampuchea (1979-95) hold the land, so this state is absent from the map between 1975 and 1993 (a loss to khmer-rouge in 1975 and a gain from people-s-republic-of-kampuchea in 1993). Cliopatria's People's Republic of Kampuchea row, which runs to 1995, overlaps the restored kingdom of 1993-1995 and should end in 1993. The Khmer Republic (1970-75) is a rename inside this dossier, not a separate state. The pages give no territorial share held by the Khmer Rouge in 1970-1974 (north-east only); the four north-eastern provinces drawn are the researcher's reading of 'all five of Cambodia's northeastern provinces'. Not on the pages and therefore not recorded: the Preah Vihear ICJ judgment of 1962 (the Thai dossier, kingdom-of-thailand, has no matching loss either), the Thai-Cambodian clashes of 2008-2011, Cambodia's border treaties with Vietnam, and the Khmer Rouge-Vietnamese war of 1977-78 (khmer-rouge dossier). No rulers strip: the Kingdom page's infobox lists Sihanouk (1953-55), Suramarit (1955-60), Sihanouk as Chief of State (1960-70) with Kossamak as ceremonial monarch, Cheng Heng (1970) but the page for the restored monarchy gives only Sihamoni's crowning in 2004. Counterparts without dossiers: khmer-rouge and people-s-republic-of-kampuchea are other parts of se-04. [Reviewer se-04-a 2026-10-19: the war 'Cambodian-Thai border conflict of 2025' was removed from wars[] because it lies outside the state's life (1953..2024; validator warning); the Cambodia page: 'In 2025, a border dispute with Thailand escalated into an armed conflict'; no border moved.]
